1: We're finally free! No more whips, no more Mr. Jones!
2: Four legs good, two legs bad! Four legs good, two legs bad!
3: Four legs good, two legs... better? Is that right? I can't remember anymore.
4: The sheep stares at you in silence.

1: The hay harvest will be twice as good now that we work for ourselves!
2: I will work harder. The windmill will be built, you'll see.
3: My hoof hurts... but Napoleon is always right. I will work harder.

1: Comrade, isn't it wonderful? The farm is ours at last.
2: Something about the dogs worries me. And where did Snowball go?
3: Boxer looks so tired. I told him to rest, but he won't listen.
4: When I look at the pigs now... I can no longer tell them apart from the men.

1: Donkeys live a long time. None of you has ever seen a dead donkey.
2: I said nothing before, and I say nothing now.
3: I could read the lettering on that van, if anyone bothered to ask.
4: Nothing ever changes. Donkeys live a long time.

1: Comrades! Rejoice! Jones is gone forever!
2: The windmill was Napoleon's idea all along. Snowball stole the plans!
3: The windmill was destroyed by Snowball's agents in the night. Traitors, all of them!
4: All animals are equal. Some are simply more equal than others.

1: The revolution has only begun, comrade.
2: The farm needs order. My dogs will keep us safe.
3: You have questions? Squealer speaks for me.
4: Napoleon does not look up from his meal.

1: Have you heard of Sugarcandy Mountain, comrade? Up there, past the clouds.
It's Sunday seven days a week. Clover grows all year round. Lump sugar on the hedges!
The pigs call me a liar. But they cannot say I'm wrong.
4: Ah, you're still here. So am I. Sugarcandy Mountain is still waiting.
Funny thing. The pigs don't chase me off anymore. They give me a gill of beer a day.
Work hard, comrade. Your reward is coming. Just... not here.
Why are you staring? Get back to work, comrade.

1: Cluck! No more eggs carted off to market. We keep our own now!
2: Napoleon wants our eggs for trade with the men. Over my dead body.
3: They cut our rations until we surrendered the eggs. Nine of us died for it.
4: The hen clucks quietly and pecks at the ground.
